craft_notes: Sthāyin: grip-never-let-go; freedom-alive (jīvanmukti in two beats). Sanskrit-first: dṛḍha-graha (FIRM-GRIP — kept); jīvanmukti (FREEDOM-ALIVE — kept ‘freedom, alive’). Rows: 9 (grip/never-let-go — holding doubled), 1 (‘alive’ closes — jīvat last: freedom breathing), 12 (śānta-vīra settle: held fast). Close: ‘freedom, alive’. Rupture: em-dash (grip commanded, then its name). Rejected: ‘living’ — killed: alive breathes; ‘hold fast forever’ — killed: never-let-go kept. Read aloud: GRIP-one-ness WITH-know-ing AND-nev-er LET-go — … THAT-grip IS-free-DOM, a-LIVE.

lines: Grip oneness with knowing and never let go —

reads_against.argmap: How is freedom won back? → Return by recognition, not effort: climb, burn, own, hold fast.
c1_essence: Return climbs, burns, owns, holds fast — freedom alive.
